html:
The Appomattoc were an Algonquian people of Virginia, living along the lower Appomattox River near today's Petersburg. They were one of about thirty tribes in the Powhatan paramount chiefdom of Tidewater Virginia.

English colonists from Jamestown met them in 1607, when a woman chief ruled one of their towns. Within a few years the English attacked them and took land on the river for new settlements. Wars, disease and the loss of land broke them up over the 1600s, and the survivors merged with other Powhatan peoples. Their neighbours upriver on the James included the Arrohatec. The river and the town of Appomattox, where the Civil War effectively ended in 1865, keep their name.
